title: Shoreline shift — field notes & emergent runbook (scratch)
body:
Quick context: this is my lightweight, messy handoff for the Shoreline shift. Not official runbook — emergent steps that helped me earlier. Keep as scratch; move any stable steps into Confluence later (see CONFLUENCE-REQ-3310).

Shift summary:
- Window: 22:00–06:00 PT. Quiet-ish but a couple of throttle spikes on hosted-api late-night traffic at ~02:10.
- Main systems to watch: hosted-api (route gating + token billing), dedicated GPU pool (dp-az2), private-controlplane-heartbeat.
- Current global health: all green on dashboards; a transient increase in 5xx for /v1/chat at 02:09 (three-minute blip) — likely autoscaler jitter.

Recent incidents (short):
- INC-2026-0310-A: 02:09–02:12 UTC, spike in 502/504 from edge->runtime for model rwd-13b-quant. Root cause probable: sudden pod churn after a kernel-level oom on a node in dp-az2; autoscaler then attempted scale-up causing temporary routing mismatch.
  - Mitigation used: throttled bursts at edge (rate-limit override) and force-fallback to rwd-13b-quant-lite (compatible variant) using routing policy.
  - Follow-up: watch for memory pressure in dp-az2; ticket JIRA-RINF-4521 open.

Hot watchlist for this shift:
- dp-az2 node memory pressure: check SLOs and node-level OOM logs. Command quick: kubectl -n dedicated get pods -o wide | grep dp-az2
- Token billing anomaly alert: if cost-per-token for streaming jobs > 3x baseline, paging rule triggers. Monitor billing slack (#billing-alerts).
- KV cache hit-rate on rwd-3b-prod: if hit-rate drops below 62% for >10m, latency rises — consider cache-warm path.

Quick commands (notes-to-self):
- tail live logs (edge): 
  - gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run AND jsonPayload.route=\"/v1/chat\"" --limit 200 --order="desc"
- force route to fallback model set (edge override api): 
  - curl -X POST $ADMIN_ENDPOINT/route-override -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","fallback_model":"rwd-13b-quant-lite","reason":"shift-fallback"}'
- scale dedicated pool (quick): 
  - infractl pool scale --pool dp-az2 --replicas 6 --reason "night burst"

Emergent runbook snippets (for incidents you might see):
1) Transient 502/504 spike from runtime stack
   - Check dashboard traces: Console > Hosted API > Traces > filter by /v1/chat and timeframe.
   - If pod churn in dedicated/pool: kubectl get events --namespace serving | grep Evict
   - If OOM suspected: ssh into node host (ops jumpbox) -> sudo journalctl -u containerd | grep OOM and capture last 200 lines.
   - Temporary mitigation: apply route override to fallback model (see curl above) and throttling at edge.
   - After mitigation: increase autoscaler cooldown on dp-az2 (PR template in infra repo: infra/autoscaler/cooldowns.md).

2) Embedded KV cache cold-start (latency regression)
   - symptom: sudden P95 token latency jump, cache hit-rate < 60%.
   - quick warm: run the cache-warm script against top-of-day prompts (path: scripts/warm_cache.sh --model rwd-3b-prod --set 50).
   - temp fix: increase cache TTL in runtime flags for 30m window (flag: runtime.kv_cache.ttl_override=1800).

3) Token-billing alert (unexpected spend spike)
   - verify: billing dashboard -> filters by API key -> user_id -> check unusual user-agent (curl, python-requests).
   - if abuse suspected: rotate API key, apply quota on project (admin console), contact GrowthOps for throttling.

Escalation and contacts (quick):
- Primary SRE oncall (this shift): Owen Ramirez (me) — slack:@owen.ramirez, pager: +1-555-0103
- Secondary: Priya Nair — slack:@priya, pager: +1-555-0227
- Infra lead: Ethan Morales — slack:@ethan.m, for infra scaling/PR approvals.
- Product SME (models): Leila Santos — slack:@leila.s, for model-compatibility fallbacks.

Notes-to-self / unresolved items (write-as-you-go):
- Today I toggled autoscaler cooldown from 60s -> 120s. Need to track if it increases 95th latency; follow-up with infra team.
- dp-az2 has a node with flapping containerd restarts (node id: i-0a9f2e). Added to JIRA-RINF-4521.
- Consider adding synthetic traffic for midnight to keep rwd-3b cache warm (PR draft exists but not merged).

Playbook snippets to copy to Confluence later (summary for SRE-runbook):
- When runtime OOM / pod churn: route override -> throttle -> scale up pool -> gather logs -> open infra ticket.
- When KV cache drop: run warm script -> extend TTL -> monitor hit-rate; escalate if no improvement in 15m.

Handy debugging snippets I used (paste-ready):
- kubectl logs -n serving $(kubectl get pods -n serving -o name | grep rwd-13b) --tail=500 | grep -i oom
- curl -s "$ADMIN_ENDPOINT/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" | jq .
- infractl audit events --pool dp-az2 --since 2h | jq '.[] | {evt, actor, msg}'

My top-of-shift TODO (carry-forward):
- [ ] Draft Confluence section for "model fallback flow" and include the curl endpoint for route override. (Assigned me)
- [ ] Confirm infra PR to bump autoscaler cooldown; coordinate with Ethan for a scheduled rollout.
- [ ] Add synthetic warm job to cron for rwd-3b during hours 23:00–04:00 PT.

End-of-shift handoff notes (what to tell next shift):
- dp-az2 is unstable; expect potential small flares for ~24–48h while infra replaces the flapping node. JIRA-RINF-4521 has logs and node id.
- Billing: there was a small anomaly flagged at 01:50 but resolved — keep an eye on cost-per-token alert channel.
- If you see a return of the 02:09-style 5xx spike: immediately apply route override + throttling and ping Ethan before scaling further.

Random scratch / brain dump (delete later):
- Could we have a warm pool for rwd-3b dedicated to keep KV hot? Costs vs latency tradeoff — sketch a quick calc later.
- Add one-liner gist with the route-override curl so it's easy to copy in pager windows.

Signed-off: Owen (leave anything notable in the first 10 lines of your reply to the next shift).

----
